# `silk/build/watch`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Running a command again each time a project's sources change, for `silk dev`.

The command runs as the leader of its own process group, so that stopping it also stops the
program it started. While it runs, SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP are held: the next look stops the
group, and [`restarting`](#restarting) answers 128 plus the signal's number. It needs macOS or Linux.

Import as `Watch` with `import silk.build.watch as Watch`.

Public declarations: 2.

<a id="packageSources"></a>

## `packageSources`

```silk
pub effect fn packageSources(root: &Path) -> List<Path>
    ! FileError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

What a package's development run watches below `root`: its `src` directory and its
`silk.toml`.

<a id="restarting"></a>

## `restarting`

```silk
pub effect fn restarting(
    program: &Path,
    arguments: &[Bytes],
    directory: &Path,
    sources: &[Path],
  ) -> i32
    ! FileError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator | &mut FileSystem
```

Runs `program` with `arguments` in `directory`, sharing the terminal and environment, and runs
it again each time a file under one of `sources` (a directory or a file) changes, stopping the
running one first. A run that ends by itself is reported, and the next change starts it again.
Directories named `build` or `node_modules`, and names starting with `.`, are not watched.
Answers 128 plus the number of the signal that stopped it, or 1 when the program cannot be
started.


Category: Build.

Profiles: `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-no-libc`.
